project_metadata.job_title: Senior Full-Stack / Platform Engineer for AI SaaS Platform
project_metadata.job_description:
We are building a confidential AI SaaS platform and need a hands-on senior technical operator who can learn quickly, hit the ground running, and help us move faster without breaking production quality.
This is not a junior role, not an agency role, and not a theory-only architecture role. We need someone who can open a complex repo, understand what matters, identify risk, fix real issues, improve tests, and help ship safely.
You will work directly with the founder on a fast-moving AI SaaS product with active frontend, backend, infrastructure, security, integration, and release-quality workstreams.
The ideal candidate has a strong track record of joining complex products, learning quickly, and becoming useful within days, not months.
The first engagement will likely involve reviewing active PRs, resolving CI failures, fixing security/dependency issues, improving frontend/backend reliability, reducing Dev/Prod risk, and helping stabilise release quality.
You must be evidence-driven. Every change needs clear proof: what changed, what was tested, what risk remains, and whether the work is safe to merge.
NDA required before detailed access is provided.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Andre, three scope questions from the front-end review. All three are decisions rather than defects, so they're yours rather than Anjali's.

1\. Is the multi-user scenario in Release 1? The invite send exists, but the front end never calls POST /account/users/accept and there's no route for the invite link, so an invited user has nowhere to land. Making it work end-to-end also needs member-list, revoke and remove on the backend: none of those endpoints exist today.

2\. "Instant access revocation" is in the product description, but with #1427 open the disconnect endpoints return success without removing the connection record. The front end handles this correctly and refuses to claim success, so the claim and the behaviour don't currently match.

3\. Anjali's per-member metering requirements (token consumption per member, usage breakdown, individual limits) are implemented only in the superadmin console under /admin. The account owner has no access to any of them. Was an owner-facing view planned for R1, or is that Phase 2?
